body.p: Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of this application in view of the foregoing amendments and following remarks.
Claims 1-11 are pending in this application and stand rejected. By this amendment, claims 1-3 are amended. No new matter has been added by this amendment. A pplicant-Initiated Interview
On behalf of the Applicant, the Attorney initiated an Interview with Examiner, which was conducted on July 1, 2024.
The Attorney presented proposed claim amendments to claims 2 and 3, and the Examiner agreed that they would overcome the Section 112 rejections.

The Attorney presented arguments with regard to the Section 102 rej ection of claim 1. One of the arguments, repeated below, was that the Applicant was serving as its own lexicographer when it recited in claim 1 that the "hand drive motors . . . [were] configured to directly drive the plurality of hands," and that the intent of "directly drive" was that there was no use of a mechanism such as a belt for transmitting a driving force. The Examiner was not persuaded by this argument or by two other arguments presented. The Attorney asked what the Examiner's view would be if a negative limitation relating to a drive belt were explicitly introduced into claim 1. The Examiner stated that he would have to see the precise language, but he did acknowledge that Hofmeister utilizes a drive belt, and that depending upon the precise language introduced, further search and consideration might be required. The Attorney noted that additional claim amendments were under consideration by the Applicant, but as the Examiner would need to see the precise language, the parties agreed that it was not timely to discuss the additional proposed amendments verbally.
Applicant is grateful for the Examiner's time and courtesy during the Interview.

Claims 2-5 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112 as allegedly being indefinite. Claim 2 recited "in which a plurality of encoders faces each other," which the Examiner considered to be unclear and indefinite. Claim 3 recited "a plurality of subframes disassembled along the motor axis," which the Examiner considered to be unclear and indefinite.
The claims are hereby amended, and the Examiner has indicated that the amendments will overcome the Section 112 rejections.
Claims 1, 6-7, and 11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by Hofmeister (USPN 6,485,250).
Claim 2 stands rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hofmeister in view of Gilchrist (US 2003/0011228 Al).
Claims 8-10 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Hofmeister in view of Kojima (US 2022/0131452).

As presented in the Telephone Interview, Applicant's first argument regarding claim 1 was that Hofmeister does not disclose "a plurality of hands . . . configured to pivot individually around a pivoting axis," for which "a motor axis to which the plurality of hands are each connected becomes concentric with the pivoting axis." The arms of Hofmeister (66, 68) [FIG. 2 and col. 3, 1. 5-10] pivot around a single axis, but the hands (effectors 38, 39) [FIG. 3 and col. 4, 1. 15-16] do not. Annotated Fig. 2 of Hofmeister shows the pivot axis about which hand (end effector 39) rotates. End effector 38 has a separate pivot axis. The annotated pivot axis for hand 39, the pivot axis for hand 38, and the motor 34 are three separate axes. Therefore, the pivot axes and the motor axis of Hofmeister are not concentric with regard to the plurality of hands.

The second argument presented in the Telephone Interview is that the drive motors of Hofmeister do not directly drive the plurality of hands. As noted above, the Examiner disagreed about the definition of the term "directly drive." However, he was open to reconsidering the claim if a negative limitation supporting Applicant's definition of the term were explicitly introduced into claim 1. Applicant therefore hereby explicitly amends claim 1 to recite that the "drive motors . . . [are] configured to directly drive the plurality of hands, respectively, without using a mechanism such as a belt for transmitting a driving force . .." Support is found in the Specification in paragraphs [0031] and [0035] as filed.

In contrast, as can be seen in at least Figs. 3 & 3A-3C of Hofmeister, and as discussed in the Specification, the drive motors 42, 44, and 46 use a series of intermediate pulleys and associated belts to eventually drive the hands. Therefore, the drive motors of Hofmeister do not directly drive the hands.

The third argument presented in the Telephone Interview is that paragraph 11 of the Office Action erred in identifying frame 32 of Hofmeister as an arm. As described in at least paragraphs [0003]-[0005] of the original specification, one of ordinary skill in the art understands articulated transfer robots as having an arm that moves a hand which supports an object. As noted above, elements 66, 68 of Hofmeister are the arms. As shown in at least Fig. 2 of Hofmeister, frame 32 is not part of the robot 24 itself and is merely used to support the robot on a car 22. Frame 32 of Hofmeister is fixed and does not contribute in any way to movement of the hand. While the Examiner was not persuaded by the first or third arguments, they are repeated here for the sake of completeness, and to preserve the argument for possible appeal.
Again, Applicant is grateful for the Examiner's attention to this application, and requests the Examiner's reconsideration in light of the amendments and arguments presented herein.

No petitions or additional fees are believed due for this amendment and/or any accompanying submissions. However, to the extent that any additional fees and/or petition is required, including a petition for extension of time, Applicant hereby petitions the Commissioner to grant such petition, and hereby authorizes the Commissioner to charge any additional fees, including any fees which may be required for such petition, or credit any overpayment to Deposit Account No. 604,560.
Please contact the undersigned for any reason. Applicant seeks to cooperate with the Examiner including via telephone if convenient for the Examiner.
An early and favorable examination on the merits is respectfully requested.
